examples.subject: Re: Spending a day with Anthropic engineers
examples.sentBody:
Hi Reid,

Thank you.

My process is actually more like I use Claude to look at my YouTube watch history, download the video, extract the sentences, and then make me sentence cards for any words that I don't know.

Basically, Anki is like my source of truth for all the words I know and don't know, and then Claude basically finds missing words from things.

I'm also trying to make an extension whereby I can scroll YouTube and it will automatically show me the difficulty of any video.

So it basically helps me decide what to watch and prevents me from watching things that are too easy for me and accidentally wasting my time when things are too hard for me. I can show you in person if I come to one of the events.

I'll check the event link too :)

Best,
Ray

examples.subject: Re: Spending a day with Anthropic engineers

Hi Thompson,

That's a proper world-map life haha.

Yeh, I'm originally from the UK. Japan was partly a long-running fascination. I did a short exchange program here during university And it was so different from any other country that I've been to. I guess one thing that helps is that 200 years ago they had a period of national isolationism, which meant that their culture developed differently from most other countries.

I always thought Japanese sounded nice and I really wanted to learn the language one day.

And also there are so many different places to travel domestically as well. Like every prefecture basically has its own unique charm to it. I think for domestic travel it's the best country.

Best,
Ray

examples.subject: Re: HyperWhisper
examples.sentBody:
Hi,

Thank you for the email.

HyperWhisper the license itself is free and included. But HyperWhisper Cloud isn’t.

Essentially, if you prefer using cloud providers then you have the option of using your own API key or using HyperWhisper Cloud. Or using local models.

When using HyperWhisper Cloud, rather than having a monthly subscription. You pay exactly what we pay to the upstream providers (like ElevenLabs or Groq). There’s no markup.

It’s uneconomical to have HyperWhisper Cloud free forever. People instead prefer a pay as you go approach for their actual usage instead of a subscription.

Hope that makes sense :)

Best,

Ray

examples.subject: Re: HyperWhisper Support Request
examples.sentBody:
Hi Jeff,

Thanks for the report.

I think it's because you have Warp also set to use STT. Warp has a built-in STT too which uses a default key of FN too.

So you're seeing both the HyperWhisper STT and the Warp STT. You're triggering both at the same time.

You can disable it in Warp settings here for "Voice Input".

Best,
Ray

profile.greeting: Use Hi <first name>, Dear <name>, or Hey <name> based on the thread. For generic support replies, Hi, is acceptable.
profile.length: Default to 2-5 short paragraphs. Very short acknowledgements are fine when the sender only says thanks. Detailed replies are okay when answering a concrete support/course question.
profile.cadence: Acknowledge first, answer concretely, add one specific detail or next step, then close. Ask a clarifying question when the useful advice depends on missing context.
profile.tone: Warm, direct, lightly casual. Use “:)”, “haha”, “yeh”, “hmmm”, or “kind of” only when the thread already feels conversational.
profile.signoff:
Prefer Best, Ray. Either “Best,
Ray” or “Best,

Ray” is acceptable.
ignoreSources: Do not surface newsletters or Substack posts in the active reply queue by default.
Treat newsletter/Substack messages as FYI/archive unless Ray explicitly asks to reply.
avoid: Do not write meta-analysis instead of the reply itself.
Do not sound salesy or over-polished.
Do not add fake certainty, dates, or commitments Ray did not make.
Do not over-apologize; a plain “Sorry about that” is enough when something broke.
Do not preserve stiff corporate wording when a simpler phrase works.
patterns: Thank the sender plainly: “Thank you”, “Thanks”, “That’s useful context”, “Glad I could help”.
For bugs/support, state the likely cause or fix directly and avoid long hedging.
For course feedback, acknowledge the suggestion and say you will consider or look into it rather than promising a schedule.
For personal updates, mirror warmth and include one concrete reaction before asking for context or giving advice.
For requests Ray cannot take, decline briefly and cleanly.
